note: NWPP KEEPER #2, PROMOTED 2026-09-20 (lane NWPP-42) BY OWNER STANDING RULING, verbatim: "Is this a recommended keeper candidate? If so plz promote. If structural integrity improves but gates regress that may still be a keeper." Structural integrity improves AND NO GATE REGRESSES, so the ruling is satisfied on its easier limb. Supersedes the ISO's only prior keeper (lane NWPP-41), pruned in this same session per rule 35 [R-PROMOTE] (a) after the year union was enumerated first per 35(b) -- {2023, 2024, 2025}, which this keeper covers in full per 35(c), NWPP having no held-out year registered -- and after audit_keepers confirmed the incoming stores resolve per 35(e). THE DETERMINATION IS **NOT-YET**, AND THIS KEEPER IS NOT A CALIBRATION. A keeper is the ISO's most structurally faithful registered run (rule 1 [R-STRUCT]); it is not a claim that the market is calibrated. NWPP is additionally PRICE UNSCORED (rubric v3.8): no admissible NWPP hourly price series exists (FINDING-nwpp-13 read NO under a pre-registered STOP gate), so C3a / C3b / C3c are NOT SCORED in any year and this run certifies no price level, shape or tail. NWPP has NO `complete` entry and NO `frontier`, and this promotion deliberately creates neither. THE RUN: the predecessor lane's frozen recipe plus EXACTLY ONE armed field, measured_coal_heat_rates=True. Bundle results/calibration/nwpp42_coalhr_span -- a COMPOSITE of three single-year shards, because rule 36 [R-YEAR-ISOLATION] (owner ruling 2026-09-19, miso-262) landed mid-lane and requires every backcast year to be solved alone in its own container. All three shards were pinned to the immutable SHA b68673a99926a554d0a9e165f5bd06b890572c02 and each pushed its FULL bundle including dispatch/<year>_P1.parquet (rule 34 [R-SHARD-PROMOTABLE] (a)); the legs are recoverable by full sha from .gitignore's nwpp42 block and from the FINDING. The parent ran NO LP (rule 32(a)). scripts/probes/_nwpp42_compose_span.py verified before composing that all 855 non-year-carried scenario_config fields agree across the three legs, that the solve-surface fingerprint is shared, and that each leg's gas_price_override matches its OWN calibration_flags.gas_prices entry. THE DEFECT: NWPP takes the legacy aggregate-fleet path (absent from CAMPD_BINNING_ISOS by owner ruling N8), and that path prices coal on eGRID's ANNUAL PLANT AVERAGE PLHTIAN / PLNGENAN -- an average over every hour the plant ran, including starts, shutdowns and deep part load. Measured against the plants' own CAMPD-metered steady-state rates the estimate is HIGH at EVERY ONE of the 12 covered plants (7,956.4 of 8,104.4 MW = 98.2 % of NWPP COAL capacity), cap-weighted 11.868 -> 11.066 MMBtu/MWh (-6.8 %), and the error is far from uniform: Hunter 13.3303 -> 10.9688 (1.2153x), North Valmy 13.1105 -> 11.3634 (1.1537x), Hardin 15.8428 -> 14.3005 (1.1078x), Wyodak 13.1065 -> 12.0467 (1.0880x) against Colstrip 10.5702 -> 10.3342 (1.0228x) and Jim Bridger 11.2457 -> 11.1511 (1.0085x). RULE 14 [R-ACCURATE] IS THE BASIS, NEVER THE RESIDUAL. The structural signature is what distinguishes it from a fitted multiplier: the correction is near-ZERO exactly where the model already reproduces the measured shape (Colstrip 1.023x, measured diurnal peak/trough 1.07) and largest where it does not (Hunter 1.215x, measured peak/trough 1.62 against a model 1.00). THE TABLE: data/raw/_processed-legacy/campd_coal_heat_rates_NWPP.csv, md5 8dd65f9e73352bcd73ef4f4ea11f35fd, derived by the NEW scripts/data/derive_campd_coal_heat_rates.py -- the COAL sibling of the nyiso-89 CT deriver -- from EPA CAMPD unit-level hourly opTime / grossLoad / heatInput over 2023-2024-2025, converted to a NET basis by the committed parasitic_load_factors.parquet (the SAME map the benchmark's net actual uses). TWO DECLARED DEPARTURES FROM THE CT DERIVER, both on physics and both fixed ex ante in the PRECOMMIT before any solve: the loaded window is a steady-state screen opTime >= 0.99 rather than a near-peak load screen, because a coal unit's NORMAL range includes part load; and fuel identification reads primaryFuelInfo rather than unitType, because at Jim Bridger, Naughton and North Valmy the coal units and the gas-converted units are BOTH boilers. Neither choice was selected by looking at a result. RULE 21 [R-DOF]: ZERO free parameters added -- build_dof_ledger emits 3 entries / 3 residual on this bundle, IDENTICAL to the two predecessor lanes. Rule 19 [R-ONE-MECH]: the measured rate REPLACES the eGRID estimate for covered plants rather than stacking on it; a plant absent from the table or flagged out-of-band keeps its eGRID value unchanged and no fallback value is invented. Rule 13 [R-MEASURED]: forward-native -- the same quantity regenerates for a forward year from the then-current CAMPD feed and responds to changed conditions. Class-gated to COAL in the fleet row loop, so it cannot reach a gas unit at a plant that has both (Jim Bridger 8066 contributes COAL and ST_GAS rows from one plant_code and only the COAL rows take it), guarded by tests/unit/data/test_measured_coal_heat_rates.py. GATE G5 / rule 1 [R-STRUCT]: authorized_price_tuning = NONE, VERIFIED FROM DISPATCH rather than asserted -- the three shared-config groups carrying non-unity bands (CC_INTERMEDIATE, CT_INTERMEDIATE, ST_GAS_INTERMEDIATE) carry ZERO NWPP energy in all three years, machine-checked by scripts/gen_nwpp42_attestation.py before the attestation was written. RULE 29(b) -- WHY THIS LANE SPENT A CONTROL SOLVE, which rule 29(b) normally forbids: rule 36 flipped MARKET_SIM_WARMSTART_XYEAR and MARKET_SIM_P1_BASIS_SEED to default OFF and rule 36(e) WITHDREW the neutrality claims that had justified them, so the predecessor keeper's committed 2024 / 2025 numbers carried a solve-path artifact of size UNMEASURED outside MISO (rule 36(f)). Form 4 could not be relied on for C4, the criterion at issue. The lane therefore solved a PAIRED PER-YEAR CONTROL on the predecessor's own recipe and differenced arm(year) MINUS ctl(year). The control bundle is NOT registered (rule 29(c)) and is gitignored, never deleted (rule 31 [R-RETAIN]). THE RULE-36 ARTIFACT, MEASURED FOR NWPP -- the lane's second deliverable, answering 36(f) for this ISO. The split is clean: ANNUAL CLASS VOLUME IS UNCHANGED (control minus predecessor keeper = 0.000 TWh for EVERY class in EVERY year, coal included) while the HOURLY allocation moves materially (max |delta| 765.2 / 817.1 / 817.9 MW, sum |delta| 1.516 / 0.915 / 0.698 TWh in 2023 / 2024 / 2025, concentrated in HYDRO and CC_REGULAR -- the flexible resources whose monthly energy budgets bind the annual total while leaving the within-year placement free). On the SCORED criteria the artifact is negligible: the control reproduces the predecessor's C4 coal r to 0.001 (0.539 / 0.547 / 0.502 against 0.539 / 0.546 / 0.502), its NRMSE exactly, and its C2 2025 coal row exactly. MISO measured up to 24.18 TWh of ANNUAL class movement; NWPP measures 0.000. The two are not comparable and neither generalises -- each lane owes its own measurement, and NWPP's is now on the record. THE GATES, differenced against the paired control. C1 fuel-mix PASS -> PASS (18/18 all, 14/14 free). C2 system volume PASS -> PASS. C4 dispatch correlation FAIL -> FAIL. C6 governance PASS -> PASS. C8 forced-energy share PASS -> PASS (D-2 reads 0.0 % forced on every class in every year -- this keeper forces NOTHING). Determination NOT-YET -> NOT-YET on {dispatch_corr} alone. NOTHING REGRESSES, and every C4 coal number moves toward the measured fleet: r 0.539 / 0.547 / 0.502 -> 0.570 / 0.559 / 0.524 and NRMSE 0.301 / 0.397 / 0.432 -> 0.292 / 0.387 / 0.408; 2023's NRMSE crosses INSIDE the 0.30 gate and C4 coal now fails on the correlation floor alone in that year. The C2 2025 coal row improves -29.3 % -> -26.4 % (SKIPPED on the preliminary EIA-923 vintage, so it gated neither way). The reported-only C5a CO2 error improves -16.0 / -23.8 / -21.5 % -> -14.4 / -23.5 / -20.6 % and changes no determination (rubric v2.9). PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS, SCORED INCLUDING THE NEAR-MISS. The PRECOMMIT predicted coal rises materially but does not close the gap (held), r improves without reaching 0.70 (held in both halves), 2023 is the risk year and may push a C1 row out of band (NOT at the gate -- C1 stays 18/18 -- but the magnitude moved; see below), zero movement outside coal (held: hydro EXACTLY flat all three years, footprint total within 0.002 TWh), and DOF unchanged at 3/3 (held). THE KILL CONDITION -- a 2025 coal move below 0.5 TWh would have made the verdict inert -- did NOT fire (2025 moved +1.110 TWh), BUT 2024 moved only +0.382 TWh, which is below that line; had 2024 been the pre-registered kill year this arm would have read inert. Named rather than glossed. C1 ROWS AT FULL MAGNITUDE, INCLUDING THE ONE THAT DEGRADES: the PRECOMMIT named 2023 the RISK year, and C1 stays 18/18 — but a row that passes can still move the wrong way, so the magnitudes are recorded rather than absorbed. Band ±min(max(2.0 % ISO-load, 3 % actual-gen), 8 TWh) and ±3 pp. 2023 COAL_BIT actual 14.594: ctl +0.390 / +0.330 pp -> arm +2.193 / +0.996 pp — THE ONE DEGRADING ROW, and the predicted one, 1.803 TWh worse inside the band. 2023 COAL_PRB -1.038 -> -0.904 and COAL_WC -0.135 -> -0.136. 2024 COAL_BIT (actual 12.832) -5.381 -> -5.350, COAL_PRB (21.030) -1.707 -> -1.356, COAL_WC (0.575) -0.342 -> -0.342. 2025 (all three SKIPPED on the preliminary EIA-923 vintage) COAL_BIT (18.210) -11.500 -> -11.268, COAL_PRB (23.635) -3.203 -> -2.325, COAL_WC (0.226) -0.160 -> -0.161. Net: five coal rows improve, three unchanged, ONE degrades. The table also SHARPENS what this keeper does not close: the coal deficit is overwhelmingly a COAL_BIT deficit in 2024/2025 (model 7.48 / 6.94 TWh against actuals 12.83 / 18.21, roughly half) and the arm moves those rows by only 0.031 / 0.232 TWh — a heat-rate correction does not reach it, and whatever closes C4 must. THE DEFECTS THIS KEEPER CARRIES, RECORDED AT PROMOTION AND ABSORBED NOWHERE. (1) C4 coal hourly shape still FAILS in all three years -- r 0.570 / 0.559 / 0.524 against a 0.70 floor. The residual driver is the one the predecessor lane routed and this lane did not attempt: the coal offer stack is BIMODAL (a must-run tranche in the money essentially every hour against a far dearer economic tranche), so most model coal is price-insensitive and a uniform heat-rate correction cannot produce the measured diurnal amplitude (measured peak/trough 1.183 / 1.237 / 1.311 against a model ~1.02). The structural successor is per-plant CAMPD binning, BLOCKED on bin_assignments_NWPP.csv, absent for every legacy-bin ISO -- the PRECOMMIT's fork (b). (2) Coal VOLUME is still materially under-dispatched: 2025 model coal 28.32 TWh against 42.26 actual. (3) The model-gen vs EIA-930 energy balance is -10.02 TWh in 2025 against a +/-3.0 tol, the served-interchange construction lane NWPP-40 declared. (4) Every NWPP-40 and NWPP-41 disclosure is INHERITED VERBATIM into this attestation and still applies: the price-unscored posture, the G-A3 amplitude miss, the 16 %-coupled hydro set, the 2025 data posture, the two-regime PRM mismatch, the demand convention and its 30 raw-feed artifacts, the interim $2,000 VOLL, the NW<->OR Tier-3 placeholder, the Colstrip / Centralia fuel-price gap, and the C1 coal-taxonomy and PRB-proxy repairs.
